questions.q: Binary equivalent of $(25)_{10}$?
Decimal value of $(11010)_{2}$?
Hexadecimal equivalent of $(200)_{10}$?
exp: $200 \div 16 = 12$ remainder $8$.
$12 = C$: result $C8$. Check: $12 \times 16 + 8 = 200$.

questions.q: How many zeros exist in 8-bit 2's complement representation?
exp: 2's complement has a single zero: $00000000$.
$10000000$ is the most negative number ($-128$), not a second zero. Contrast 1's complement, which has two zeros.

questions.q: Octal equivalent of $(1011011)_{2}$?
exp: Group by $3$ from the right: $1$ $011$ $011$.

questions.q: POS form of 2-input XOR (F=0 on rows 0 and 3)?
exp: Row $0$ ($00$): maxterm $(A+B)$. Row $3$ ($11$): maxterm $(\bar{A}+\bar{B})$.
AND the zero-rows: $(A+B)(\bar{A}+\bar{B})$.

questions.q: Output of a NAND gate with inputs $1, 0$?
exp: AND gives $1 \cdot 0 = 0$; NAND inverts to $1$.
NAND is $0$ only when ALL inputs are $1$.

questions.q: A 2-to-1 MUX with $S=A, D_{0}=0, D_{1}=B$ realises?
exp: $Y = \bar{S}D_{0} + SD_{1} = \bar{A}\cdot 0 + A\cdot B = AB$.
Feeding $0$/$B$ turns the select into an AND control.

questions.q: Half adder with $A=1, B=0$. Carry output?
exp: Carry $C = AB = 1 \cdot 0 = 0$.
Sum is $1$ ($1 \oplus 0$); carry needs both inputs $1$.

questions.q: $A + \bar{A}B$ simplifies to?
exp: Covering theorem: if $A=1$ the result is $1$; if $A=0$ the result is $B$.
So $A + \bar{A}B = A + B$.

questions.q: D latch with enable $EN=0$?
exp: Disabled latch closes its feedback loop: $Q$ frozen.
$EN=1$ is the transparent state where $Q$ follows $D$.

questions.q: How are flip-flops clocked in a ripple counter?
exp: Asynchronous chain: each $Q$ clocks the next stage (with all $T=1$).
Delay accumulates ($n \times t_{pd}$) — the price of simplicity.

questions.q: Flip-flops needed for a MOD-5 counter?
exp: Truncated counter resets at the first unused code $101$.

questions.q: A 4-bit ring counter holds $1000$ and shifts right. Next state?
exp: The single $1$ moves one position right.
$1000 \to 0100$. Four one-hot states cycle.

questions.q: When does a Moore machine output change?
exp: Moore output $Z = f(state)$ is driven by the registered state.
It changes only on clock edges — clean, at the cost of an extra state.

questions.q: $2mA$ enters a node; $0.5mA$ leaves through one branch. Current in the other branch?
exp: KCL: in = out, so $2 = 0.5 + x$.
$x = 1.5mA$ leaving.

questions.q: Half-wave rectifier with peak $V_{p}$ and no filter. DC output?
exp: Average of one half-hump over the full cycle: $V_{p}/\pi \approx 0.318V_{p}$.
Full-wave doubles it to $2V_{p}/\pi$.

questions.q: A bridge rectifier is fed with $50Hz$ AC. Ripple frequency?
exp: Full-wave uses both humps: two pulses per input cycle.
Ripple $= 2f = 100Hz$. Half-wave would stay $50Hz$.

questions.q: A silicon diode has $0.3V$ forward bias. Its state?
exp: Below the $\approx 0.7V$ knee, conduction is negligible.
Treat as OFF. Reverse breakdown needs large reverse volts.

questions.q: Maximum power transfers to the load when?
exp: Matched load: $R_{L} = R_{th}$.
Then $P_{max} = V_{th}^{2}/(4R_{th})$ at 50% efficiency.

questions.q: Price rises $25\%$, then falls $20\%$. Net change?
exp: Equivalently $1.25 \times 0.8 = 1.0$ — a quarter up, a fifth down cancel.

questions.q: Pipe A fills a tank in $4h$; a leak alone empties it in $6h$. Net fill time with both open?
exp: Signed rates: $1/4 - 1/6 = (3-2)/12 = 1/12$ per hour.
Invert: $12h$ to fill.

questions.q: A $300m$ train at $15$ m/s passes a pole. Time taken?
exp: Point object: own length only.

questions.q: Boat speed $10$ km/h, stream $6$ km/h (down/upstream pair $10$/$6$). Still-water speed?
exp: Still water $= (down + up)/2 = (10+6)/2 = 8$ km/h.
Cancel first: divide by $3! = 6$.

questions.q: Two fair coins tossed. P(both heads)?
exp: Independent AND multiplies: $1/2 \times 1/2 = 1/4$.

questions.q: Odd days in a leap year?
exp: Ordinary years leave $1$.

questions.q: Average of $2, 4, 6$?
exp: Total $12$ over $3$ items: $12/3 = 4$.

sections.title: Section A — Fill in the blanks

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: A 3-variable K-map has ___ cells.
exp: Cells = truth-table rows = 2^3 = 8.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: An 8-to-1 multiplexer has ___ select lines.
exp: 2^n inputs need n selects; 8 = 2^3.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: A 4-bit SISO shift register takes ___ clock cycles for a bit to travel in to out.
exp: One stage per clock; latency equals the stage count.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: The knee (cut-in) voltage of a silicon PN diode is about ___ V.
exp: Si conducts past ~0.7V (≈0.3V for Ge); ideal model uses 0V.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: A full-wave bridge rectifier uses ___ diodes.
exp: Four-diode bridge needs no centre tap; each diode sees PIV = Vp.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Size of a char variable in C is ___ byte(s).
exp: char is one byte by definition.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: In C, 7/2 evaluates to ___.
exp: Integer division truncates; use 7.0/2 for 3.5.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: strcmp() returns ___ when the two strings are equal.
exp: Zero means equal; negative/positive give byte-wise order.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: HCF of 12 and 18 is ___.
exp: Common divisors 1,2,3,6 — greatest is 6 (LCM is 36, product 216).

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: P(6) on a fair die is ___ (fraction).
exp: One favourable face out of six equally likely.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: In a K-map, a group of 2 cells eliminates how many literals? What shapes are illegal?
questions.model: A group of 2 (= 2^1) kills 1 literal. Groups must be power-of-2 rectangles (1/2/4/8); diagonal, L-shaped or 3/6-cell groups are illegal.
exp: Group of 2^k kills k literals: pair 1, quad 2, octet 3.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Write the carry-out equation of a full adder and name what it computes.
questions.model: Cout = AB + Cin(A⊕B) = AB + BCin + ACin — the majority function (1 when two or more of A,B,Cin are 1).
exp: Sum S = A⊕B⊕Cin is odd parity; carry is majority vote.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: What D flip-flop input is needed for the transitions 0→1 and 1→0?
questions.model: D equals the desired next state: 0→1 needs D=1; 1→0 needs D=0 (D excitation is trivial: D = Q+).
exp: No excitation table needed for D — the next-state column IS the D map.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: What is a Thevenin equivalent? How is Rth found (independent sources)?
questions.model: Any linear two-terminal network = Vth (open-circuit voltage) in series with Rth. Rth: deactivate independents (short voltage sources, open current sources) and look back from the terminals.
exp: Norton twin: IN (short-circuit current) in parallel with RN = Rth.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: For Thevenin/superposition analysis, how are independent voltage and current sources deactivated?
questions.model: Voltage source → short circuit (0V). Current source → open circuit (0A). Dependent sources stay ON always.
exp: Open a voltage source or short a current source breaks the analysis.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Contrast while and do-while loops in one line each.
questions.model: while checks first — body may run zero times. do-while checks last — body runs at least once.
exp: Entry-tested vs exit-tested; VEDA output traces exploit the difference.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Contrast malloc() and calloc() in one line each.
questions.model: malloc(n) returns n raw bytes (uninitialised garbage). calloc(n,sz) returns n×sz zeroed bytes. Both need a NULL check and exactly one free().
exp: realloc resizes via a temp pointer (keeps the old block on failure).

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Evaluate 1<<3 in C and state the general rule.
questions.model: 8. Left shift by k multiplies by 2^k (unsigned): 1<<3 = 8.
exp: Right shift divides; shifts ≥ width are undefined.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: SP is Rs 600 after 20% profit on CP. Find CP.
exp: Profit lives on CP: build SP by ×(1+p%), recover CP by ÷.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Equal distances at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. Average speed?
questions.model: Harmonic mean 2ab/(a+b) = 2×40×60/100 = 48 km/h (always below the 50 arithmetic mean).
exp: Equal TIMES average arithmetically — check what is equal first.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Downstream 10 km/h, upstream 6 km/h. Stream speed?
questions.model: Stream = (down − up)/2 = (10−6)/2 = 2 km/h. (Still water = (10+6)/2 = 8.)
exp: Down = u+v, up = u−v; add for boat, subtract for stream.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: State the log laws for log(ab) and log(a^n).
questions.model: log(ab) = log a + log b (product to sum). log(a^n) = n·log a (power comes down).
exp: Plus change of base log_b(a) = log a / log b.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Minimise F(A,B,C) = Σ(0,1,4) with a K-map. Show the groups and the minimal SOP.
questions.model: Ones at 000, 001, 100. Pair m0–m1 (00−): ĀB̄. Pair m0–m4 (−00): B̄C̄. All ones covered: F = ĀB̄ + B̄C̄. Check m5(101): ĀB̄=0 (A=1), B̄C̄=0 (C=1) → 0 ✓; m2(010): both 0 ✓; m7: both 0 ✓.
exp: Overlap on m0 is encouraged; diagonal groupings would be illegal.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: A decade (MOD-10) counter uses 4 flip-flops. At what code must it reset, and what is the minimal clear logic?
questions.model: First unused state is 10 = 1010. Clear when Q3·Q1 = 1 (the two 1-bits): CLR = NAND(Q3,Q1) for active-low clear (equivalently AND for active-high). Minimal 2-input product — no need to decode all four bits.
exp: Reset at M itself (first UNUSED code), never at M−1.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: (i) A toggle chain of 3 stages divides clock by what factor? (ii) In a synchronous binary up-counter, what is T0?
questions.model: (i) Each toggle stage halves frequency: 2^3 = 8. (ii) The LSB flips every clock: T0 = 1 always (T1 = Q0, T2 = Q1Q0, …).
exp: Bit k toggles when all lower bits are 1 — the carry-chain rule.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: A 12V source drives 2kΩ in series with a 4kΩ shunt to ground. Find the Thevenin equivalent at the shunt top node.
questions.model: Vth = open-circuit (divider) voltage = 12 × 4/(2+4) = 8V. Deactivate (short 12V): Rth = 2k‖4k = (2×4)/6 = 1.33kΩ. Equivalent: 8V source in series with 1.33kΩ.
exp: Open for volts, short the source for ohms, then reconnect the load.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Trace fact(4) where fact(n) = n·fact(n−1) with base fact(1) = 1. Give the unwinding, the result, and the number of calls.
questions.model: Calls: fact(4)→fact(3)→fact(2)→fact(1) = 4 calls. Unwind: fact(1)=1; fact(2)=2×1=2; fact(3)=3×2=6; fact(4)=4×6=24. Result 24.
exp: Each call pushes a frame; the base case starts the return cascade. Missing base = stack overflow.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: (i) a[i] equals what pointer expression? (ii) With char s[] = "hi", what is sizeof(s)?
questions.model: (i) a[i] = *(a+i) — indexing is scaled pointer addition. (ii) "hi" stores h,i,\0 = 3 bytes, so sizeof(s) = 3 (strlen would be 2).
exp: sizeof counts the terminator; strlen counts chars before it.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: x = 12 (1100₂). (i) Evaluate x & (1<<2). (ii) Evaluate x & ~(1<<3).
exp: Test with &mask, set with |mask, clear with &~mask, flip with ^mask.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A+B finish a job in 4 days, B+C in 6 days, A+C in 12 days. How long does B alone take?
exp: Pair-system trick: halve the total, subtract the pair without B.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown. P(sum = 9)?
questions.model: Pairs: (3,6),(4,5),(5,4),(6,3) = 4 of 36 equally likely outcomes. P = 4/36 = 1/9.
exp: List ordered pairs — (3,6) and (6,3) are distinct outcomes.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A clock gains 5 minutes per hour. When 12 true hours pass, what time does it show?
questions.model: 65 shown minutes per 60 true minutes. 12 true hours show 12×65/60 = 13 hours (12h36m gain → displays 13:00 if started at 12:00).
exp: Fast-clock math: scale indicated time by (60+gain)/60.
